consensus_findings.description: Task 3.2, design.md D4, work-packages.yaml description, and plan-findings.md Round 7 explicitly require synchronizing the feature branch with current main before task 3.2 so that existing helper skills/tests/_shared/openspec_paths.py (change_dir()) and guard skills/tests/openspec_paths/ are consumed without package-owned writes.

Task 3.2 and design.md D4 explicitly mandate fixing the archive-unsafe test path in test_state_artifacts_guide.py via change_dir(ROOT, CHANGE_ID) from openspec_paths to preserve test stability after archival.
Task 3.3 and work-packages.yaml verification step 1 explicitly execute the OpenSpec path-stability test guard (skills/tests/openspec_paths) alongside --base main context-impact validation.

The base-relative context-impact surfaces (documentation, decisions, capabilities, semantic_code) accurately match the affected files, and the single-package scope (wp-state-artifacts-docs) remains coherent with explicit write_allow and lock constraints.
The package does not create or own shared path infrastructure; read_allow already permits consuming it, while write_allow remains limited to the approved documentation and test surface.
Task 3.2 specifies change_dir(ROOT, CHANGE_ID) and task 3.3 plus package verification run both state-artifact and OpenSpec path-stability tests after branch synchronization.
Full --base main context-impact validation passes with capabilities, decisions, documentation, and semantic_code declared and only the schema-required API stub rationalized.

The package correctly consumes the shared helper and guard without owning them. design.md D4 forbids package-local copies; tasks.md 3.2 Coverage forbids creating or copying path infrastructure inside this package; plan-findings.md Round 7 states the existing write allowlist remains correct because the documentation package does not create, copy, or own those inputs. write_allow still covers only docs, the six skills, mirrors, skills/tests/state-artifacts/**, pyproject.toml, and the change directory—not skills/tests/_shared/openspec_paths.py or skills/tests/openspec_paths/.

The archive-unsafe design.md lookup is explicitly owned by unchecked task 3.2, not left as a silent plan gap. Coverage requires resolving the design artifact with change_dir(ROOT, CHANGE_ID) and preserving the eight-stage assertion after archival; design.md D4 makes the same SHALL for any OpenSpec change-artifact lookup. Current implementation still pins openspec/changes/write-durable-state-artifacts-guide/design.md at test_state_artifacts_guide.py:83 with no openspec_paths import; that is pending 3.2 work, and the main-landed guard is exactly the suite that would fail that literal pin after sync.

Base-relative context-impact remains coherent with the declared surfaces. work-packages.yaml runs validate_context_impact.py with --base main and declares documentation, decisions, capabilities, and semantic_code, while rationalizing only the schema-required no-contract OpenAPI README stub. That matches proposal Impact (guide/index, generated docs/decisions/skill-workflow.md, modified capability skill-workflow, tests/pyproject) and the Round 6/7 plan-findings amendments that replaced the single-file --changed-file probe.

Single-package scope stays coherent with the sync-and-consume model. design.md Scope and Concurrency keeps one sequential documentation package with an explicit allowlist and forbids repository-wide write globs; work-packages.yaml declares only wp-state-artifacts-docs with depends_on: [] and the same documentation-only write surface. Round 7 clarification does not expand that surface to own openspec_paths; sync is a git prerequisite, not a package-owned write.
